parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct or gender expression, and no documented traveler-facing exposure: no border screening, facility bans, custody rules or police targeting appear in the record. That rules out tiers 1–2. But the country offers no protections, no LGR, documented societal stigma, a 2018 NGO report of some identity-based violence, and — critically — a weak rule-of-law environment (coup, torture, impunity), so any harassment or assault a trans visitor suffers likely finds no remedy. Dated data (2012/2018) and unresolved violence prevalence add uncertainty; absence of evidence is not safety. Extrapolating from decriminalisation plus stigma plus thin recourse places this near the 0.55 anchor: lawful presence, generally tolerated, but recurring hostility without reliable correction, below jurisdictions with working remedies and above criminalising or targeting states.
